build:workspace.description: Establish the Story's worktree and branch
build:workspace.purpose: Every step that reads or changes the Task's code works in one tree on the Story's branch

records.name: worktree
records.holds: the Story's worktree

records.name: branch
records.holds: the branch checked out in the worktree, a string

records.name: defaultBranch
records.holds: the repository's default branch, a string or null

adds.when: the Task's surfaces include web-ui and its design source is bundle or cds
the Task's type or a label is in the infrastructure vocabulary

build:design-source.description: Select the design source the Task's web UI is built from
build:design-source.purpose: A cds bundle the owner supplied for the Task's artifact is the design the build uses and is audited against

records.name: design
records.holds: { designSource, bundle, buildSpecs }: the design source used, the bundle directory or null, and the build spec paths

build:infra-intent.description: Author the provisioning intent of the infrastructure Task
build:infra-intent.purpose: The tests and the code of an infrastructure Task are written to concrete resources, stacks and cross-stack references

records.name: provisioning
records.holds: { provisioningIntent, affectedStacks }

build:regression-assess.description: Find the existing requirements the code this Task edits already meets
build:regression-assess.purpose: Earlier requirements stay covered: the tests are written and run against the cumulative scope, not only this Task

records.name: regressionPrevious
records.holds: the requirements and mappings recorded before this Task

records.name: regressionPlan
records.holds: the impact scope the regression-impact-assessor wrote

build:regression-review.description: Review the regression scope against the requirement sources
build:regression-review.purpose: The scope is approved by a reviewer that did not write it

records.name: regressionPlanReview
records.holds: the regression-coverage-reviewer's review of the scope

adds.when: the review names a blocking finding, so it does not approve the scope: the regression-impact-assessor is given the review, and the corrected scope is reviewed again with that review

build:regression-review.limit: It adds no correction after two corrections of the scope in this run; build:regression-validate then fails with regression-plan

build:regression-reassess.description: Correct the regression scope from its review
build:regression-reassess.purpose: The reviewer named findings in the scope, and the assessor that wrote it corrects them

records.name: regressionPlan
records.holds: the corrected impact scope the regression-impact-assessor wrote

build:regression-validate.purpose: The scope is complete and approved before any test is written, and its requirement sources are bound

records.name: regressionScope
records.holds: { requiredKinds }: the test layers the scope requires

adds.when: the validation fails because the scope's review, written by an earlier run of the workflow, did not approve it: the regression-impact-assessor corrects the scope from that review, the corrected scope is reviewed, and it is validated again; the step records nothing

build:baseline.description: Run the setup the approved regression plan declares for the tree, then resolve the repository's suite command and run the suite before any change
build:baseline.purpose: The command the build is judged by is the one the repository declares, it runs on a tree prepared as the reviewed plan states, and the tests failing before the Task are known

records.name: suiteCommand
records.holds: the command that runs the whole suite, a string

records.name: baseline
records.holds: { exitCode, summary, failing, tail, relayFile }: the suite run before any change

adds.when: always: one build:red-write per test agent the contract's surfaces call for, then the run that judges them

build:red-write.purpose: The Task's acceptance criteria are encoded as tests that fail before the code exists

records.name: testFiles
records.holds: the test files the agent created or changed, a list of paths

records.name: redConfirmed
records.holds: whether the agent saw its tests fail as intended, a boolean

build:red-check.description: Run the suite and judge whether the new tests fail cleanly
build:red-check.purpose: Red holds only when a new test fails, no test file fails to load and no other test regressed

records.name: redRun
records.holds: { exitCode, summary, failing, tail, relayFile, reasons }: the suite run and why Red does not hold, when it does not

records.name: testPrint
records.holds: { files, treeDigest }: the git blob hash of each test file and the digest of the work tree

adds.when: Red does not hold: each test agent is given the suite result, and the suite is judged again

build:red-check.limit: It fails with red-unsatisfied when four checks in this run have not shown Red, and with no-progress when the suite fails exactly as it did at the check before

build:select-implementers.description: Select the implementers whose specialties cover the Task
build:select-implementers.purpose: The code is written by the fewest agents whose specialties cover the change, in build order

records.name: implementers
records.holds: the implementer agent names, in the order they work

records.name: sharedCapabilities
records.holds: the shared capabilities the Task must use, read with atw-matrix uses --ids for the matrix ids the Task states: a list of { id, name, provides: [{ id, behaviour, consumersMust, interface }], providedBy: [{ name, kind, repository }] }

adds.when: always: one build:implement per selected implementer, then the run that judges them

build:implement.purpose: The failing tests pass with the minimum production change

records.name: changedFiles
records.holds: the files the implementer changed, a list of paths

records.name: testIssues
records.holds: the tests the implementer names as standing between the code and the contract, a list of { testId, kind, reason, contractRef }

records.name: upstreamMissing
records.holds: what must exist outside the Task before the suite can pass, a list of { what, evidence }

build:green-check.description: Run the suite and judge whether it is green
build:green-check.purpose: The Task is built only when the repository's whole suite exits 0 and the implementers left the tests as they were written

records.name: greenRun
records.holds: { exitCode, summary, failing, tail, relayFile }: the suite run

records.name: testPrint
records.holds: { files, treeDigest }: the git blob hash of each test file and the digest of the work tree

adds.when: the suite is not green and an implementer named tests that stand between the code and the contract
the suite is not green and no named test awaits a ruling: each implementer is given the suite result

build:green-check.limit: It fails with green-modified-tests when an implementer changed a test file, with blocked-upstream when an implementer named something outside the Task, with no-progress when no file changed and the suite fails exactly as at the check before, and with green when eight checks in this run since the implementers were selected have not shown a green suite

build:test-ruling.description: Rule on the tests the implementers named, with tdd-unit-test-generator
build:test-ruling.purpose: A test that contradicts the contract is changed by the agent that owns the tests, never by an implementer

records.name: testDecisions
records.holds: one ruling per named test, a list of { testId, action, reason }

records.name: testFiles
records.holds: the test files the agent changed, a list of paths

build:reuse-audit.description: Check the changed files against the shared capabilities the Task must use
build:reuse-audit.purpose: A behaviour a shared library, layer, chassis or service provides is used from it and written nowhere in this repository

records.name: reuseAudit
records.holds: { clean, violations, judgment, unchecked }: whether the audit found no violation; each violation as text, those atw-matrix check-reuse found and each definition the shared-capability-reviewer ruled a duplicate; each definition the reviewer ruled on with its ruling and reason; and the relied-on behaviours that have no use signal

adds.when: the first audit of this run finds violations: each implementer is given them, the suite is judged, and the audit runs again

build:reuse-audit.limit: It fails with reuse-violation when violations remain at the audit that follows this run's correction, and with reuse-audit when atw-matrix check-reuse does not rule or the shared-capability-reviewer leaves a definition unruled

build:refactor-snapshot.description: Record the work tree as it is before the refactor
build:refactor-snapshot.purpose: A refactor that is repeated or undone goes back to the tree the green suite ran on, not to a tree an unfinished refactor changed

records.name: refactorSnapshot
records.holds: the git tree id of the work tree before the refactor, a string

build:refactor.description: Refactor the code the implementers changed
build:refactor.purpose: The change is left clear and free of duplication without changing behavior

records.name: refactorChangedFiles
records.holds: the files the refactor changed, read from git against the snapshot

records.name: refactorReverted
records.holds: whether the refactor gave up and the tree was put back at the snapshot, a boolean

build:refactor-check.description: Run the suite after the refactor
build:refactor-check.purpose: A refactor that turns the suite red is undone

records.name: refactorRun
records.holds: { exitCode, summary, failing, tail, relayFile }: the suite run

adds.when: the suite is red after the refactor and the tree has not been restored
the suite is green and the Task's web UI has design source bundle or cds

build:refactor-check.limit: It fails when the suite is still red after the tree was restored to the snapshot

build:refactor-restore.description: Restore the work tree to the snapshot taken before the refactor
build:refactor-restore.purpose: The suite went red after the refactor

records.name: refactorRestored
records.holds: { restored, evidence }

build:cds-audit.description: Audit the changed web UI against its design source
build:cds-audit.purpose: The UI styles nothing outside the design system the Task was built from

records.name: cdsAudit
records.holds: { verdict, findings, scriptVersion, violations, gaps }: the audit verdict, the count of violations and gaps, and each as text

adds.when: the first audit of this run finds violations: each implementer is given them, the suite is judged, and the audit runs again

build:cds-audit.limit: It fails with cds-audit when violations remain at the audit that follows this run's correction, and with blocked-upstream when the design system lacks something the UI needs

build:docs-audit.description: Audit which documents the change leaves stale
build:docs-audit.purpose: Documentation is brought up to date in the same commit as the code

records.name: staleDocs
records.holds: the stale documents, a list of paths

records.name: docAssignments
records.holds: the stale documents by the documentation agent that owns their kind, a list of { agent, docs }

adds.when: documents are stale: one build:docs-write per documentation agent assigned

build:docs-write.description: Update the stale documents with {docAgent}; the documentation-accuracy-reviewer checks them
build:docs-write.purpose: The audit named documents the change leaves stale

records.name: updatedDocs
records.holds: the documents the agent updated, a list of paths

build:final-suite.description: Run the suite a final time
build:final-suite.purpose: Nothing is committed unless the whole suite exits 0 on the tree as it will be committed

records.name: finalRun
records.holds: { exitCode, summary, failing, tail, relayFile }: the suite run

build:regression-map.description: Map each requirement in scope to the tests and commands that prove it
build:regression-map.purpose: Every required test layer of the approved scope names concrete tests and a command that runs them

records.name: regressionMapped
records.holds: the final mapping the regression-impact-assessor wrote

build:regression-map-review.description: Review the regression mapping against the tests as written
build:regression-map-review.purpose: The mapping is approved by a reviewer that did not write it

records.name: regressionMappedReview
records.holds: the regression-coverage-reviewer's review of the mapping

adds.when: the review names a blocking finding, so it does not approve the mapping: the regression-impact-assessor is given the review, and the corrected mapping is reviewed again with that review

build:regression-map-review.limit: It adds no correction after two corrections of the mapping in this run; build:regression-verify then fails with regression-coverage

build:regression-remap.description: Correct the regression mapping from its review
build:regression-remap.purpose: The reviewer named findings in the mapping, and the assessor that wrote it corrects them

records.name: regressionMapped
records.holds: the corrected final mapping the regression-impact-assessor wrote

build:regression-verify.description: Run the mapped regression runs, each after its setup, and record their evidence
build:regression-verify.purpose: The commit carries fresh per-test evidence for every requirement the change can affect

records.name: regressionEvidence
records.holds: the verification result and the evidence of each mapped run

adds.when: the verification fails because the mapping's review, written by an earlier run of the workflow, did not approve it: the regression-impact-assessor corrects the mapping from that review, the corrected mapping is reviewed, and it is verified again; the step records nothing

build:commit.description: Commit the Task to the Story's branch
build:commit.purpose: The built Task lands on the branch its Story deploys from

records.name: commit
records.holds: the head of the Story's branch after the commit, a string

deploy:mechanism.description: Ask what the Story's repository publishes and deploys
deploy:mechanism.purpose: A repository publishes a package, deploys with CDK, both or neither, and the deploy runs only what applies

records.name: mechanism
records.holds: { repository, publishes, publishCommand, deploys, reason }

deploy:workspace.purpose: The deploy runs from the tree that holds the Story's built Tasks

records.name: worktree
records.holds: the Story's worktree

records.name: branch
records.holds: the Story's branch, a string

adds.when: the repository publishes a package
the repository deploys with CDK and publishes no package

deploy:publish.purpose: The repository publishes a package other repositories install

records.name: publishedHead
records.holds: the commit the package was published from, a string

records.name: deployFailure
records.holds: { step, output, stacks }, recorded only when the publish failed

adds.when: the publish succeeded and the repository deploys with CDK
the publish failed

deploy:publish.limit: It fails when three fixes of this Story's deploy have already run

deploy:synth.purpose: The cloud assembly names the stacks and the SSM parameters the deploy needs

records.name: assembly
records.holds: the CDK cloud assembly

records.name: deployFailure
records.holds: { step, output, stacks }, recorded only when the synth failed

adds.when: the synth succeeded
the synth failed: after the fix the package is published again when the repository publishes one, then the app is synthesized again

deploy:synth.limit: It fails when three fixes of this Story's deploy have already run

deploy:ssm-check.description: Check that the SSM parameters the stacks read exist
deploy:ssm-check.purpose: A stack that reads a parameter another Story's deploy writes cannot deploy before that parameter exists

records.name: ssmParameters
records.holds: the parameter names the stacks read, all present, a list of strings

adds.when: every parameter exists

deploy:ssm-check.waits: a parameter the stacks read does not exist yet

deploy:deploy.description: Deploy the stacks to AWS dev
deploy:deploy.purpose: The Story's Tasks are built and its stacks can be deployed

records.name: deployOutput
records.holds: { exitCode, tail }: the exit status of the deploy and the last part of its output

adds.when: always

deploy:verify.description: Verify that every stack reached a completed status and the worktree is clean
deploy:verify.purpose: The deploy counts only when CloudFormation reports every stack created or updated

records.name: stacks
records.holds: the status of each stack, a list of { name, status, reason }

records.name: deployFailure
records.holds: { step, output, stacks }, recorded only when the deploy or its verification failed

adds.when: the deploy or its verification failed: after the fix the package is published again when the repository publishes one, then the app is synthesized again

deploy:verify.limit: It fails when three fixes of this Story's deploy have already run

deploy:fix.description: Fix the failed deploy on the Story's branch
deploy:fix.purpose: A publish, synth, deploy or verification of the Story failed

records.name: fix
records.holds: { cause, changedFiles, testsPassed, commit }: what the story-deploy-fix workflow returned

deploy:fix-author.description: Diagnose the failure and fix it in the worktree, with deploy-failure-fixer
deploy:fix-author.purpose: The cause of the failed deploy is found in its output and corrected in the Story's code

records.name: fixCause
records.holds: the cause the agent found, a string

records.name: fixTestCommand
records.holds: the command that runs the synth assertion tests, a string that may be empty

deploy:fix-verify.description: Read what the fix changed from git and run the synth assertion tests
deploy:fix-verify.purpose: What the fix changed and whether its tests pass are measured, not taken from the agent's report

records.name: fixChangedFiles
records.holds: the files the fix changed, read from git status, a list of paths

records.name: fixTestsPassed
records.holds: whether the synth assertion tests exited 0, a boolean

deploy:fix-verify.limit: It fails with no-change when the fix changed no file

deploy:fix-commit.description: Commit the fix to the Story's branch
deploy:fix-commit.purpose: The redeploy runs from a committed tree

records.name: fixCommit
records.holds: the head of the Story's branch after the commit, a string

deploy:commits-ahead.description: Count the commits the Story's branch has that the default branch lacks
deploy:commits-ahead.purpose: A Story whose branch holds no commit has nothing to compare, review or merge

records.name: commitsAhead
records.holds: the number of commits ahead of the default branch, an integer

adds.when: the branch holds commits

deploy:built-version.description: Record what the Story built against the effective architecture
deploy:built-version.purpose: The effective architecture describes what is deployed before the Story's pull request opens

records.name: built
records.holds: { stage, differences, builtFiles }: what the built-version workflow returned, with counts in place of lists; nothing is recorded in the matrix for it

deploy:built-snapshot.description: Fingerprint the architecture and keep a copy of section 2
deploy:built-snapshot.purpose: What each agent writes in the architecture is measured, and the owner's constraints are put back if they change

records.name: constraintsBefore
records.holds: { exists, digest, gitStatus, kept }: the fingerprint of section 2 and where its copy is kept

records.name: treeStart
records.holds: the fingerprint of every architecture file before the comparison

deploy:built-compare.description: Compare the code on the Story's branch with the effective architecture
deploy:built-compare.purpose: Each difference between what was built and what the architecture shows is recorded as a built view

records.name: differences
records.holds: the differences found, a list of { element, itemId, effectiveViews, built, citations, file }

records.name: builtFiles
records.holds: the built views written, a list of absolute paths

records.name: treeCompared
records.holds: the fingerprint of every architecture file after the comparison

adds.when: the comparison recorded differences

deploy:built-correct.description: Correct the effective architecture to match what was built, with architecture-maintainer
deploy:built-correct.purpose: The effective architecture differs from what the Story built, or a review found the correction wanting

records.name: architectureUpdate
records.holds: { changedFiles, createdFiles, deletedFiles, matched, constraintIssues, contradictions, summary }: every pass together, with the files measured from the tree

records.name: changedSinceLast
records.holds: the files this pass changed since the pass before, a list of paths

records.name: treeLast
records.holds: the fingerprint of every architecture file after this pass

deploy:built-correct.limit: It fails when it wrote in section 2 or outside the effective architecture, and when a pass that answers findings changed no file

deploy:built-review.description: Review the correction of the effective architecture, with architecture-conformance-reviewer
deploy:built-review.purpose: The correction is checked by a reviewer that did not write it

records.name: conformance
records.holds: { conforms, findings, reviewedFiles, matchedBuiltViews }

adds.when: the review has findings
the correction conforms

deploy:built-review.limit: It fails when the correction does not conform after two corrections that answered findings

deploy:built-approve.description: Set the corrected architecture files to effective
deploy:built-approve.purpose: A reviewed correction becomes the effective architecture

records.name: approval
records.holds: { promoted, unchanged }: how many files were set to effective and how many already were

deploy:built-remove.description: Remove the built views the effective architecture now matches
deploy:built-remove.purpose: A built view exists only while the effective architecture differs from what was built

records.name: removedBuiltViews
records.holds: the built views removed, a list of absolute paths

deploy:built-remove.limit: It fails when a built view remains that the effective architecture does not match

deploy:pull-request.description: Push the Story's branch and open its pull request
deploy:pull-request.purpose: The Story's deploy is verified and its branch holds commits

records.name: pullRequest
records.holds: the pull request URL, a string

deploy:mark-verified.description: Set what the Story built verified in the matrix once its CI checks pass
deploy:mark-verified.purpose: The Story's test has passed when its deploy to AWS dev was verified working and every check on its pull request's head commit passed; what it built is then built and tested, before and apart from the merge, which decides nothing about verified

records.name: matrixVerified
records.holds: { commit, entries, unmatched }: the head commit whose checks passed, the ids that carry the flag and the ids that matched no entry; commit is null and nothing is marked when the pull request merged with a check that did not pass

deploy:mark-verified.waits: a check on the pull request's head commit has not finished, or failed while the pull request is open

deploy:merge-wait.description: Wait for the Story's pull request to merge
deploy:merge-wait.purpose: The Story closes only when its code is on the default branch

records.name: pullRequestState
records.holds: the state GitHub reports for the pull request, the string MERGED

deploy:merge-wait.waits: the pull request is open and not merged

deploy:close.description: Close the Story and remove its worktree and local branch
deploy:close.purpose: A Story with nothing left to deploy or merge is done

records.name: closed
records.holds: true
